messages:
maria: quick flag 1 — ruby minimal sampleapp onboarding is flaking on token refresh with a 401 on the first request in many runs. anyone else seeing intermittent 401s?
jon: yep reproduced locally. looks like a race where the refresh thread swaps credentials and a request picks up the old Authorization header.
maria: repro: `bundle exec ruby examples/minimal.rb --refreshable-token` then immediately call /generate. sometimes get 401 then retry succeeds.
lee: share the client init? could be header cached on connection object.
maria: snippet: 
```
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], use_refreshable: true)
resp = client.generate(prompt: 'hi')
```
we're probably building the header once and not re-evaluating when token changes.
jon: our adapter caches headers to avoid per-request allocs. fine for static keys but breaks when token mutates mid-flight.
olivia: options: add a mutex around refresh so only one thread refreshes and others wait, or compute Authorization per-request by calling a proc. Mutex reduces concurrency during refresh; proc adds a tiny alloc but simpler.
sara: for the sampleapp, we should document the recommended pattern (pass a proc/lambda), and add a regression test that simulates concurrent requests during refresh.
maria: opened PR with the proc approach when use_refreshable: true (small change). https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/pull/47
rb-ci-bot: CI: ruby-sampleapp/minimal-onboard 1 failure on matrix ruby-3.2 (flaky 401) 1 rerun started.
jon: PR looks okay; please add a concurrent test to catch regressions.
maria: added a threaded test that swaps the token mid-request and asserts no 401s, pushed commit.
lee: also add a note in docs/quickstart.md recommending: 
```
client = Redwood::Client.new { fetch_fresh_token }
```
so people don't wire ENV directly into the client.
olivia: +1. Dedicated customers could hit this under short burst patterns.
sara: include a changelog bullet in the gem release notes mentioning the change in token semantics.
maria: will squash and add changelog. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
jon: once CI is green i'll merge and backport to maintenance.
lee: tracking: we might add an opt-in header-caching toggle for ultra-low-latency scenarios. opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/issues/62
maria: CI passed, merged, changelog included. closing the loop :tada:
